h: Gardens, castle country and the drive home
p: Set aside two to three hours for Fyvie if you want the house, the loch and a nose round the gardens. The walled garden is worth hunting out, with a focus on Scottish fruit and vegetables, and it's a peaceful contrast to all those towers and portraits. Visit in late spring or summer and it's at its most colourful.

Aberdeenshire calls itself Scotland's Castle Country, and Fyvie is a brilliant anchor for a castle-hopping day. Haddo House is a short drive to the south-east, with its Georgian front and lavish Victorian rooms. Head west instead and Huntly Castle, a grand ruin with remarkable carved stonework, makes a dramatic stop. Just outside Turriff, Delgatie Castle is a long-standing home of the Clan Hay and another option for castle collectors.

Turriff itself is a friendly market town, handy for a bite to eat and a wander before you head home. Push north and you'll soon reach the Moray Firth coast at Banff and Macduff, where Duff House, a grand William Adam mansion, sits beside the river and the coast offers sea air and harbours.

This is rural country, so a car is the easiest way to link everything up. Distances aren't huge, but country roads wind about, so allow a bit longer than the sat nav suggests. Pick two stops rather than five, take your time, and you'll come home feeling you've properly seen this corner of Scotland.
